title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 169 (When finder of thing commonly on sale may sell it)

content.overview: Section 169 provides that when a thing which is commonly the subject of sale is lost, if the owner cannot with reasonable diligence be found, or if he refuses, upon demand, to pay the lawful charges of the finder, the finder may sell it— (1) when the thing is in danger of perishing or of losing the greater part of its value; or (2) when the lawful charges of the finder, in respect of the thing found, amount to two-thirds of its value.
content.glance: Finder may sell a commonly saleable lost thing if the owner cannot reasonably be found or refuses to pay lawful charges, when the thing is perishable or losing value, or when charges amount to two-thirds of its value.
content.study: When a thing which is commonly the subject of sale is lost, if the owner cannot with reasonable diligence be found, or if he refuses, upon demand, to pay the lawful charges of the finder, the finder may sell it— (1) when the thing is in danger of perishing or of losing the greater part of its value; or (2) when the lawful charges of the finder, in respect of the thing found, amount to two-thirds of its value. Current-law framing: limited power of sale in specified circumstances.

essentialIngredients: Thing commonly the subject of sale
Owner cannot with reasonable diligence be found or refuses to pay lawful charges

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 169 allows the finder to sell a lost thing commonly the subject of sale if the owner cannot with reasonable diligence be found or refuses on demand to pay the lawful charges, and either the thing is in danger of perishing or losing the greater part of its value, or the lawful charges amount to two-thirds of its value.
examples: Perishable goods or high relative charges permit sale in the stated circumstances.
distinctions: Limited statutory power of sale for finders; not a general right.
problemApplication: Identify commonly saleable thing and owner issues.
keyTakeaways: Finder may sell in limited circumstances where owner cannot be found or refuses to pay and the thing is at risk or charges are high.
